business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Desktop 3D Printers and Resin Filaments

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (Private Interest Foundation under Law 25 of 1995)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law with Common Law-inspired fiduciary and corporate trust principles
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA) in force 2012
Panama-United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (DTA) signed 2019, in force 2020
Central American-Dominican Republic FTA (CAFTA-DR) observer/related trade protocols

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 2015 on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism, as amended by Executive Decrees 163 of 2016, 405 of 2017, and 33 of 2020; Resolution 281 of 2019 of the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF); Law 25 of 1995 (Private Interest Foundations); Law 5 of 2008 (beneficial ownership reporting); Executive Decree 363 of 2015 (obligations of regulated non-financial professionals); Supreme Decree 47 of 2013 (foundation registry regulations).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foundation Charter (Acta Constitutiva / Estatutos) executed before notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panama Notary Public (Notario) and Registro Público de Panamá
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Panama is party to the 1961 Hague Convention; apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of origin country or Panama's Dirección General de Protocolo)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Same-end Petition for Registration of the Foundation (Ficha de Registro)
Certificate of Good Standing / Movable Assets Declaration (when later filing initial accounts)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization if origin country is not a Hague Convention member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Statement and Source of Funds Declaration (Declaración de Beneficiario Final)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered Agent (abogado notario or licensed law firm) and UAF for regulated filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for certified copies used abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (if incorporator is represented)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against UN Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC SDN and sectoral lists, EU consolidated sanctions, Panama's National Anti-Money Laundering List (Decree 405 of 2017), and the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) public statements. PEP screening of all beneficial owners, directors, foundation council members, and protectors, with enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons, family members, and close associates as defined by Law 23 of 2015, Article 36 et seq.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Sistema de Información del Registro Público de Panamá (SIRP) online consultation at registropublico.gob.pa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory requirement that the foundation name must be in Spanish, English, or another alphabet using Latin characters, transliterated into Spanish script if necessary; must not be identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered entity; must not violate public order or morality; names may be expressed in any language but must be transliterated for registry indexing.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Foundation – when used in a way implying a regulated charitable entity without authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the registered agent or incorporator may file a written solicitation of reconsideration with the Registro Público's Dirección General de Registro within five business days, attaching the registry search certificate and a written argument of distinctiveness; if rejected, an administrative appeal (recurso de apelación) may be filed before the Dirección General within ten business days, and ultimately before the full Registro Público board or via the Contencioso-Administrativo court at the Supreme Court of Justice. A new name reservation may be filed concurrently without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Generally permissible as the statutory seat (registered office) for a PIF provided a licensed resident agent (abogado notario or law firm) furnishes an address in Panama; however, the foundation's central administration or management must align with the act to avoid sham characterization by tax authorities. For e-commerce sellers using Stripe and Shopify, the registered agent address is sufficient; no physical office, staff, or equipment is legally required. Virtual office services for mailing and legal notices are accepted, but the resident agent's address appears in the public registry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% quantified risk of unannounced on-site inspections for a low-risk e-commerce foundation, primarily triggered by the registered agent's general inspection obligations under the UAF, or if the foundation is selected for a statistical inspection program; inspections concentrate on physical record-keeping, original books or digital ledger storage, and evidence of the foundation's asset custody. A fully virtual PIF without any local operational presence has a materially lower (approx. 5-8%) inspection probability absent a risk trigger.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations, as amended by Law 49 of 2015; Articles 1-25; Executive Decretes regulating RUC registration
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá), Foundations Section
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Acta Constitutiva) executed before a Notary Public and inscribed in the Private Interest Foundations Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital, but founding charter must declare a sufficient initial endowment; standard prudent endowment for bank account opening is USD 10,000, which may be held in escrow
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the initial endowment of USD 10,000 is subscribed by the Founder and funded before the Public Registry; the registered office at [City, Republic of Panama] is adopted for filing and administrative purposes; the persons named below are appointed as Foundation Council members and Protector for a one-year term; the Council members are authorized to open a bank account, sign bank instructions, and engage the registered agent; the Council delegates the protector to file all regulatory notices and tax registrations. The resolution is effective immediately and entered into the minutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Legal Entities Names Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit written application to the Public Registry requesting certification that the proposed foundation name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity. Obtain the official name certificate before proceeding.
required_dossiers: Copy of founder's passport or ID
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file an administrative reconsideration or submit an alternate name for a new certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Certified Panamanian Attorney acting as registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Attorney drafts the Foundation Charter including founder, Foundation Council members, Protector, purpose, duration, registered office address, initial endowment, and amendment rules. All parties review and initial every page.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any formal deficiencies identified by the attorney before signing; recirculate the amended draft.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All parties appear before the notary to execute the Foundation Charter. The notary converts the charter into a public instrument, assigns a protocol number, and issues the first copy (testimonio) for registry use.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises defects, have the parties correct signatures or annex clarifications and re-notarize.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Foundations Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized testimonio and duplicate to the Foundations Section together with registry stamp tax payment. Verify that the registrar enters the foundation into the legal persons register and issues a provisional inscription certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a 'nota preventiva' or observation, file corrective documentation within the statutory term, pay any outstanding balance, and request expedited review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Official Foundation Certificate and Ficha
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Certification Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request the certified 'Ficha de Fundación' evidencing legal existence, registered address, and officers. This document is used as proof of incorporation for banking and tax appointments.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate lists inaccurate data, present supporting documents and petition the registry to issue a corrected 'certificación de vigencia'.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Identification Number (RUC) Registration with DGI
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the foundation certificate and registered agent authorization to the DGI to obtain the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC). Select the e-commerce economic activity under ISIC 4791 and register for monthly or annual income tax filing as applicable.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney for tax filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI queries missing documents, provide corrected documentation within 15 days and request an in-person or virtual follow-up appointment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce and Industries (MICI) – not applicable for online e-commerce under ISIC 4791 without physical industrial premises
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – online retail of 3D printers and consumables; no physical manufacturing or sales establishment in Panama

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – activity is online retail only with no discharge, no manufacturing, and no land alteration; future warehousing may require Category II registration if floor area exceeds thresholds
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or solid waste generation attributable to the online business. If warehousing or fulfillment is later established, compliance with Resolution AG-0626-2016 wastewater discharge limits and Law 7 of 2018 waste handling standards is required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for remote e-commerce operations. If a physical office or warehouse is opened, a fire safety inspection by the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá and a municipal occupancy permit will be required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI — General Directorate of Revenue), an integrated directorate of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (Ministry of Economy and Finance) of the Republic of Panama; taxpayer digital portal SETA (Sistema de Administración de Tributos) at https://seta.mef.gob.pa and official DGI guidance portal www.dgi.gob.pa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) incorporated under Law 25 of 1995 obtains its tax identity as follows: (1) ensure valid registration of the foundation and its Pacto Fundacional at the Registro Público de Panamá, with the statutorily required resident secretary/agent; (2) file the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) inscription request through the SETA online portal or at a DGI service office using the official registration forms; (3) attach the certified copy of the registered foundation charter, identification documents (cédula or passport) of the foundation council members/directors, and proof of Panamanian fiscal domicile; (4) declare the intended economic activities (online retail of 3D printers and consumables) and choose the applicable ITBMS compliance (general or pequeño contribuyente); (5) upon RUC issuance, activate SETA electronic credentials and enrol for facturación electrónica (mandatory e-invoicing); (6) obtain the municipal Aviso de Operación from the relevant alcaldía before commencing sales; (7) pay the annual PIF registry fee (approximately USD 300) to the Public Registry, which is separate from DGI tax obligations. Non-resident founders and beneficiaries are not required to obtain personal Panamanian tax IDs; DGI requires designation of a locally resident taxpayer representative to receive electronic notifications.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope — the PIF is a separate juridical person taxed at entity level exclusively on Panama-source income under the territoriality principle (Código Fiscal Article 693). Panama-source retail profits from online sales to Panamanian consumers are subject to corporate ISR at the standard 25% rate; foreign-source income (export sales with offshore delivery, foreign passive investment income) falls outside Panamanian tax jurisdiction. The PIF is not eligible for US-style pass-through or check-the-box election in Panama and is not a Tax_Exempt_Zone vehicle; however, a PIF that holds assets and carries on no Panamanian commercial activity is fiscally dormant — it has no ISR or ITBMS registration duty, while remaining subject to the annual foundation registry fee.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate a check-the-box entity classification regime. Available statutory elections relevant to a commercial PIF: (i) the simplified Pequeño Contribuyente ITBMS regime for eligible small taxpayers whose annual gross income does not exceed the statutory cap (approximately USD 150,000); (ii) corporate income-tax group consolidation for affiliated Panamanian companies (Law 8 of 2010); (iii) optional accelerated depreciation of fixed assets; (iv) the Multinational Company Headquarters (SEM) incentive regime for qualifying regional logistics/management platforms (not applicable to pure online retail); (v) simplified deemed-income methods available to small taxpayers. Panama has no hybrid-mismatch election; BEPS-type hybrid outcomes are constrained by general anti-abuse principles and the criminal tax-fraud provisions of Law 76 of 2019.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS — Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (Panama's VAT/GST on the transfer of movable goods and the provision of services), governed by Law 15 of 1995 as amended by Law 8 of 2010 and subsequent DGI regulations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: USD 0 — no statutory minimum economic-turnover threshold exists; every person habitually selling movable goods or rendering services in Panama must register for ITBMS prior to commencing operations. The simplified Pequeño Contribuyente regime applies to eligible taxpayers with annual gross income not exceeding approximately USD 150,000, functioning as a compliance-simplification threshold rather than an exemption. All fiscal thresholds are expressed in USD because the Panamanian Balboa is pegged 1:1 to the US dollar and USD is the circulating legal tender.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) is phased in for all RUC holders: the PIF must obtain DGI e-invoicing credentials and issue each invoice through either the free SETA billing module or a DGI-certified service provider (PSFE), obtaining near-real-time online authorization (pre-validation) that embeds the DGI-consecutive numbering, electronic signature, and QR fiscal code. No physical fiscal timbrado remains for general-regime taxpayers. Sales data transmitted through Shopify/Stripe payment rails must be reconciled on the merchant-of-record e-invoice declared in the monthly ITBMS return (Form 209); payment gateway settlements do not substitute for e-invoicing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: ITBMS 0% applies to (i) export of tangible goods: goods sold to a non-resident buyer and physically removed from Panamanian customs territory, evidenced by the validated customs export declaration and transport document; and (ii) export of services: services rendered from Panama to a non-resident recipient whose economic benefit is received exclusively outside Panama and whose consideration is paid from abroad, under the service-export zero-rating conditions codified by Law 8 of 2010. For the PIF's online retail of 3D printers and resin filaments, domestic deliveries to Panamanian consumers are taxable at 7%; shipments to foreign customers with a non-Panamanian delivery address qualify for 0% only where the customs export declaration (DUA or express-courier export manifest) correctly identifies the PIF (or its appointed customs agent) as exporter and the foreign buyer's payment is received on the foundation's bank account. Shipping and logistics services included in an export transaction follow the zero-rating of the underlying goods; standalone services delivered to local Panamanian customers remain taxable at 7%. Panama imposes no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline because USD is legal tender and no exchange controls exist; the 180-day parameter below is the prudential evidentiary-retention benchmark for the documents substantiating the zero-rating claim.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DUA (Declaración Única Aduanera) validated by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export of the goods from Panamanian customs territory
Commercial invoice and packing list matching the zero-rated e-invoice issued to the foreign buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/MT103 payment receipt from the non-resident buyer
Signed export contract or purchase order identifying the non-resident buyer and applicable Incoterms
Express-courier export manifest where dispatches are made through FedEx/DHL/UPS or similar carriers
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI and ANA automatically cross-verify e-invoice data, export declarations, courier manifests, and bank remittance certificates; detected mismatches trigger desk audits and can lead to retrospective clawback of the zero-rating benefit. If the zero-rating claim is disallowed, DGI assesses ITBMS at the 7% rate on the gross export value, plus moratory interest and the statutory 10% late-payment surcharge. False or manufactured export documentation exposes the PIF to fines ranging from 50% to 200% of the omitted tax and, under Law 76 of 2019, criminal liability for tax fraud (defraudación tributaria) with custodial penalties of up to approximately five years, extended where the defrauded amount exceeds statutory thresholds or an organized false-invoicing scheme is used; additional consequences include disqualification of responsible directors and publication of the sanction. The exporter of record is jointly and severally liable for clawback where the goods are diverted back into Panamanian local consumption or where the foreign buyer's remittance certificate is fabricated.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No central bank of issuance exists for Panama. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the de facto regulator for banking, market conduct, and foreign-exchange service providers. Monetary policy and dollar-liquidity management are functionally delegated to the U.S. Federal Reserve System because Panama is fully dollarized.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Unrestricted convertibility applies to both current-account and capital-account transactions. The U.S. dollar is legal tender and the Panamanian balboa is a nominal unit pegged 1:1 with no circulating notes. Profit remittances, foreign shareholder distributions, and capital repatriation require no exchange-control authorization. Only ordinary AML/KYC documentation, tax-formality, and OFAC/sanction screening obligations apply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion requirement exists. Panamanian law allows full retention, collection, and usage of USD export receipts, including on-line retail sales, without a statutory deadline or conversion percentage. This reflects the absence of a domestic monetary authority and the full-dollarization regime.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with material legal constraints. Panama does not issue a standalone Electronic Money Institution (EMI) license; therefore offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, or Mercury can only serve as ancillary payment-processing channels, not as the PIF's principal Panama-domiciled banking relationship. When used, the EMI account is typically hosted in a separate jurisdiction (U.S., U.K., Ireland, or Malta) and is treated by the SBP and Panamanian revenue authorities as a foreign financial account rather than a domestic bank account. The PIF must still maintain at least one operational account with an SBP-licensed commercial bank to satisfy legal domicile, tax ID, and administrative requirements under Income Tax Law and Law 25 of 1995.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for first-time PIF account openings where the beneficial owner or an appointed signatory exercises transactional control. Most SBP-regulated banks require at least one controller—defined as a beneficial owner holding >10% or any signatory—to appear in person at the bank's office in Panama City for a documented KYC interview. Remote opening is permissible in practice only for (i) second-generation relationships where the PIF already maintains an active account with the same banking group, (ii) regulated PIFs introduced by an SBP-licensed trust company or law firm with an established sponsorship relationship, or (iii) applicants using a notarized and apostilled power of attorney naming a resident Panamanian attorney-in-fact, subject to video verification and certified copies of all constitutional documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PIF exhibits low economic substance (no physical office, no payroll, no demonstrable commercial operation in Panama) and is perceived as a pure offshore shelf vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply of: current registered office lease agreement in Panama; website and e-commerce storefront SSL certificate; supplier contracts with 3D printer manufacturers and filament wholesalers; logistics agreements (DHL, UPS, FedEx); transaction history from Shopify/Stripe payment settlement showing continuous order flow; quarterly management accounts; economic substance declaration filed with the relevant authority; insurance certificate for business goods in transit; and a detailed business plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner or controlling signatory is resident in a high-risk or sanctions-affected jurisdiction, or is a Politically Exposed Person (PEP).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Clean OFAC/UN/SSI screening report; independent wealth-source documentation (real estate registry, tax records, business profit distribution certificates); separate bank reference letter from the applicant's existing bank; sworn statement of no criminal record; compliance certificate from a nominated Panamanian compliance officer; PEP status disclosure and risk-mitigation memo; professionally prepared CV and business background report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection is sourced from a cryptocurrency exchange or unregulated payment processor, creating an unclear provenance risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full KYC/AML certificate from the digital asset service provider; bank statements of the crypto exchange account showing the origin of funds; chainalysis or blockchain analytics report; forum pending or concluded inbound-transfer records to the PIF's USD bank account; narrative explaining the conversion from digital assets to fiat; ownership relationship of the wallet(s) holding the assets; and reference to the PIF's constitutional capital clause.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce activities are classified as cross-border retail with a high volume of micro-transactions, raising suspicion of layering or receivable structuring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Export invoices or order records from Shopify/WhatsStore; shipping provider manifests; product serial numbers or lot numbers; refund/chargeback log with banking settlement statements; customer geolocation data confirming end-user retail nature; inventory-cost match analysis from 3D printer suppliers; and proof of platform-level seller verification from Stripe and Shopify Payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The PIF uses nominee directors, a registered agent, or shareholder proxies that obscure effective control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal nomination agreement with the registered agent; original founding deed and Public Registry authentication; letter of consent signed by nominee directors; beneficial ownership register submitted under Panama's Law 23/2015 (AML); independent confirmation letter from the resident agent that the disclosed beneficial owner exercises ultimate control; and financial authorization matrix signed by all account signatories.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections into the PIF's Panamanian operational account are executed via SWIFT MT103 using the 'OUR' charge option to ensure full credit. The USD funds may originate from a foreign shareholder, a founder, or an intercompany account. The wire narrative must state the economic purpose, e.g., 'Capital Contribution / Aporte de Capital – Non-Remunerated Equity Injection', and reference the PIF's registration number. Although Panama imposes no exchange-control filing, the receiving SBP-licensed bank will perform OFAC and internal compliance screening; therefore the originator's bank should provide a covered bank reference letter and underlying security documents. To tag funds cleanly, use the UETR (Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference) and place the PEP-eligible purpose code 'NCLG' (or the respective SWIFT 'Nature of Payment Code' for capital/equity) in the narrative. In case of USC correspondent-forwarded wires, the final credit is made in USD on a same-day or next-day basis.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments to 3D printer and consumable suppliers are cleared over the existing correspondent network using SWIFT MT103 for standard wire disbursements. For larger scheduled purchases, a Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) under UCP600 is opened via the PIF's local bank through SWIFT MT700, with the beneficiary bank's account credited in USD. Trade settlement may also be supported by documentary collections (MT400) or an irrevocable Standby LC (MT799/MT760) when prepayment terms require assurance. Payment instructions must contain a clear purchase order number, proforma invoice reference, and the physical goods description to satisfy both bank AML and supplier-facing treasury controls. Panama is a fully dollarized jurisdiction; therefore the bulk of settlement uses U.S. dollar correspondent clearing via Fedwire/CHIPS, with the offshore catering for EUR/CNY settlement executed through the PIF's bank's foreign-currency branch or via multi-currency account narration.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EUR foreign-exchange forward contracts executed through an SBP-licensed Panamanian bank under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement; because the local currency is USD, no local ringgit-style NDF is required.
USD/CNY offshore NDFs transacted via an authorized international bank or money-broker in Panama or the United States, with the legal contract expressly governed by New York law or English law.

USD/CNY cross-currency swaps (floating-to-fixed or floating-to-floating) for suppliers invoicing in CNY, provided the counterparty is a licensed bank or an A-rating financial institution and the exposure is designated as trade hedge.
Zero-premium cost-reduction structures (collar, participating forward) for EUR and CNY payable flows, permissible as they represent genuine hedging of identified commercial invoices.
Currency options (European-style USD call or USD put on EUR/CNY) obtained from an SBP-regulated bank, exercised only for the contracted invoice amount, and never used as a speculative position.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (Tax Única) and DGI information schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Autoridad Nacional de Ingresos Públicos (ANIP), formerly Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each calendar year; foundation incorporated after 30 June pays 50% (USD 150) for the formation year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge plus monthly fiscal interest on late payment; after three consecutive years of non-payment the Registro Público may administratively declare the foundation inactive and strike it off; restoration requires payment of arrears, penalties, and registry fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Declaration (Declaración de Beneficiarios Finales / RBF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: ANIP-Beneficial Ownership Registry (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales) web portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within the RUC-assigned compliance month (staggered schedule in the first half of the year); any change in foundation council, protector, or beneficiaries must be declared within 30 calendar days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of USD 500 to USD 5,000 for omitted or inaccurate declarations; tax clearance certificate (paz y salvo) may be withheld until compliance is remedied.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial income tax on Panamanian-source income only; foreign-source income derived by a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) is fully exempt. The PIF is subject to a flat annual franchise tax of USD 300 in lieu of corporate income tax where no local-source commercial activity is conducted. Online exports and sales to foreign customers routed through Stripe/Shopify Payments are treated as foreign-source and thus outside the Panamanian corporate income tax base. Reduced rates of 15% apply to taxable income brackets below USD 200,000 for small businesses under applicable DGI regulations, but the headline rate remains 25%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 745 (Declaración de Renta Anual) filed electronically via Panamá DGI SIT/e-Tax portal (Dirección General de Ingresos, Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the fiscal year-end. For calendar-year taxpayers, the return must be filed on or before 31 March of the following year. The DGI publishes an annual filing calendar with specific dates based on the taxpayer's RUC termination digit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income derived from Panamanian-source activities, including retail sale of 3D printers, resins, filaments, and consumables delivered to Panama customers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only income from customers located in Panama. Export sales to foreign end users, even when facilitated through an online store, are foreign-source and excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total allowable deductions: cost of goods sold, shipping, inventory, merchant fees (Stripe/Shopify), administrative expenses, registered agent fees, and depreciation on equipment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate deductions only to Panamanian-source gross income. Common international costs may be allocated using a direct-ratio method; retain supporting invoices and bank statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income: Box 1 minus Box 2. Negative balances are eligible for carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the PIF earns no Panamanian-source income, enter zero. The PIF must still file the annual return if registered for tax purposes, alongside payment of the annual franchise tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax at 25% on net taxable income. Alternative Minimum Tax (CAIR) at 4.5% of gross income may apply where gross income exceeds USD 1.5 million.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute tax only on the amount in Box 3. Verify whether the reduced rate for small taxpayers applies to the first USD 200,000 of taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits against income tax: foreign tax credits, ITBMS credits on local purchases, advance payments already made on Form 730.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned PIF, no Panamanian foreign tax credit is available on foreign-source income because such income is exempt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or amount carried to the tax payment voucher. Payment must be made by Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) to the Panama Treasury.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no local tax remains after credits, the box is zero. Failure to pay the annual franchise tax of USD 300 is a separate delinquency that must be cleared before issuing a solvency certificate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 745 triggers a fine of USD 50 to USD 500 and monthly late-payment interest at 1.5% on outstanding tax. Fraudulent underreporting of Panamanian-source income exposes the PIF to an additional penalty of 50% of the omitted tax and possible criminal tax evasion charges under Article 771-F of the Panama Tax Code.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 730 (Anticipo de Impuesto sobre la Renta) filed quarterly via Panamá DGI SIT/e-Tax portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on or before the fifteenth day of the month following each fiscal quarter (April 15, July 15, October 15, and January 15 for calendar-year taxpayers).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimated Panamanian-source taxable income for the quarter.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a PIF whose e-commerce revenue is predominantly foreign, the estimate is typically zero. Maintain a breakdown of shipping destinations for audit trail.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance tax payment computed by applying the 25% corporate rate to line A, with quarterly apportionment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If line A is zero, the advance is zero. Overpayment of the annual franchise tax is not creditable against income tax because it is a flat fee.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total prior quarterly advance payments made within the same fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify prior electronic payment vouchers and retain the DGI stamped receipts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount due for the current quarter: Line B less Line C. A positive balance must be paid immediately.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No withholding tax is imposed on PIF distributions from exempt foreign-source profit, so no adjustment is made for dividend withholding.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file Form 730 and pay the quarterly advance incurs a fine of 10% of the unpaid advance, up to USD 250, plus monthly interest at 1.5%. Continued delinquency may lead to the DGI's automatic assessment and forced collection through embargo.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% on dividends paid from Panamanian-source profits already subject to corporate income tax; 10% on dividends paid from exempt or foreign-source profits when distributed by a Panamanian corporation. PIF distributions to beneficiaries are not legally characterized as dividends and are exempt from Panamanian withholding tax when the underlying income is foreign-source or otherwise exempt under territorial taxation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A PIF seeking treaty benefits must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (Certificado de Residencia Fiscal) from the DGI after confirming its tax status as a Panamanian tax resident. The beneficiary or payee must submit the application using DGI Form 200 (Solicitud de Certificado de Residencia Fiscal). The payer must complete the DTA relief request on the same form and retain proof of the treaty rate, a beneficial ownership declaration, and a copy of the recipient's tax residency certificate. The documentation must be kept for at least five years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Panama applies a 12.5% withholding tax on royalty payments sourced in Panama for the use of intellectual property within the country, and a 10% withholding tax on interest sourced in Panama. These rates may be reduced under applicable tax treaties, commonly to 5% or 10%, subject to filing the treaty relief application and demonstrating beneficial ownership.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 200,000: taxpayers with related-party transactions exceeding USD 200,000 in a fiscal year must file Annex 805 (Declaración de Precios de Transferencia) and maintain a full Local File. If cross-border related-party transactions reach USD 200,000, a Master File is also required.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not maintain a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime equivalent to the UAE or BVI. However, the DGI and Panama courts apply a substance-over-form doctrine to distinguish legitimate PIFs from artificial arrangements. To avoid recharacterization as a sham, the PIF must satisfy real commercial substance: physical or virtual presence, a registered agent in Panama, a board of council members that convenes, maintained accounting records, and a demonstrable business rationale for holding the online retail operations. Failure to demonstrate substance may lead to the nullification of the foundation and the imposition of full income tax, interest, and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting Panamanian-source online sales (deliveries to Panama customers) from Form 745 or understating gross receipts while claiming full exemption as a PIF on foreign-source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax evasion under Article 771-F of the Panama Tax Code is punishable by imprisonment of 2 to 5 years and a fine of 50% to 100% of the evaded tax. Civil liability includes the duty to pay all omitted tax plus monthly interest of 1.5% and a procedural surcharge of up to USD 5,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the PIF, including the council members and the resident agent who signs the tax return, are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax. A fraudulent intent may lead to criminal proceedings against the natural-person director, the suspension of their residency status, a travel ban, and up to 5 years of imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the PIF as a sham to conceal true ownership while failing to maintain any substantial commercial activity, carrying no accounting records, and using the foundation structure solely to hide foreign-sourced e-commerce income from the beneficial owner's home tax authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI and courts may disregard the legal personality of the foundation under the substance-over-form doctrine. All income of the foundation is recharacterized as taxable income of the beneficial owner; Panamanian-source business income is taxed at 25%, and fines of 50% may be imposed. The foundation's registration may be cancelled under Law 25 of 1995.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The protector and council members face personal civil liability for fraudulent conveyance. In serious cases, directors may be charged before the Panamanian criminal courts for fraud, resulting in pecuniary sanctions, real estate embargo, travel restriction, and imprisonment of up to 6 years when the scheme is used to evade foreign tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to implement basic customer identification when processing Stripe or Shopify Payments; allowing the online store to be used for laundering criminal proceeds through the sale of 3D printers/resins or by receiving payments from sanctioned entities; failing to report suspicious payment patterns to the Panamanian Financial Intelligence Unit (UAF).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 23 of 2015 (amended), non-financial commercial entities that engage in online payment processing are obliged to establish AML protocols. Violations attract administrative fines from USD 10,000 up to USD 1,000,000, suspension of the commercial license, and the freezing of bank and payment accounts. Criminal money laundering is punishable by 5 to 10 years of imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly execute or facilitate a money-laundering transaction through the PIF are subject to criminal liability as principals. They may face civil forfeiture of personal assets, a travel ban blocking departure from Panama, and imprisonment from 5 to 10 years. The foundation's assets are subject to confiscation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Engaging in cross-border related-party transactions with the PIF's parent company or sister entities (e.g., sourcing resins from a related supplier) without filing Annex 805 when transactions exceed USD 200,000, or using internally derived prices that are not at arm's length.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A tax correction may be imposed by the DGI, adjusting taxable income to the arm's length amount. Applicable penalties include an addition to tax of 10% to 40% of the adjusted amount, plus monthly interest of 1.5%. Failure to file the documentation concurrently with the annual tax return leads to an autonomous fine of up to USD 30,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The DGI may attribute the adjustment to the foundation only, but directors who knowingly prepare fraudulent transfer pricing documentation face personal liability for the additional tax and fines. Repeated non-compliance may result in criminal sanction for fraud, including a travel ban and imprisonment up to 5 years.
